## The Source Base

### The Pool

**Three sweeps retrieved 29,246 records of which 22,875 were distinct.** The shared rejection store removed 1,530. The subject gate admitted 9,787 and refused 11,558. Deduplication by title and year removed a further 298, leaving **9,467 records, every one of which is cited** across 14 clusters. A further 142 definitions are hand-written, being 79 primary documents and encyclopaedic anchors and 63 back-references to earlier articles in this series.

By source the admitted set is 8,849 from the journal and conference index, 606 from the national reports server and 332 from the defence technical registry. **The reports server is thin and that is a fact about this subject rather than about the sweep.** The plug nozzle was studied between the late nineteen fifties and the late nineteen seventies by government laboratories and their contractors, who wrote report numbers, and a third sweep was run specifically in that vocabulary and against those organisations by name. **The primary-reference pass is where this imbalance has to be answered rather than noted.**

### The Homonyms, Measured Before the Sweep Was Written

**Every central noun of this subject is owned by another field**, which is a different situation from the previous several articles, where the collisions were proper nouns and a qualifier fixed them. A bare probe of each term was run against the bibliographic index before a single query was composed.

`spike` returns Spike Jonze, Spike Lee, the spike harp, the spike fiddle and the spike lute in a music dictionary, wheat spikes, neural spike trains and the coronavirus spike protein, with nothing mechanical in ten results. **`wake closure` returns fatigue crack closure in the crack wake**, an entire metallurgical literature using both words in its own sense, together with a school closure, two newsroom closures and a book called `Conquistador's Wake`, and no rocket result at all. `open wake` returns Wake Forest University, `In Gettier's Wake` and an emergency medicine journal. `closed wake` belongs to wind-farm wake steering. `area ratio` is owned by cardiology, returning mitral and tricuspid regurgitant jet area ratios. `thrust coefficient` is owned by wind turbines. **`gas generator` is owned by nineteen-seventies coal gasification**, nine of ten results being Department of Energy quarterly reports on the BI-GAS and TRI-GAS processes. `annular` belongs to borehole flow and to radiology. `throttling` is a dictionary headword, a graph-theory invariant and a chapter of a shell-scripting book. **`altitude compensation` returns altitude physiology and a 1976 paper on compensating a carburettor**, which is the same idea in a different machine and is not this literature. And a bare `nozzle` returns ten results, one of them a diesel injector diagram.

**So every pattern in this article's gate pins its noun with a second noun.** The compounds measured clean and productive are `truncated plug nozzle`, `aerospike nozzle`, `expansion deflection nozzle`, `plug nozzle altitude compensation` and `linear aerospike`. The only single words that survive are `aerospike`, `turbopump` and `truncated plug`, and `aerospike` still returns a dictionary headword and a fish.

**The proper nouns are worse than the physics.** `ARISE` returns a Victorian poem in `Notes and Queries`, two dictionary headwords, a hymn, a stereoelectronic chemistry paper, Christopher Reeve, **and a real European atmospheric-dynamics research infrastructure of the same name**, which no general-science guard can refuse. `ABL` returns Abl tyrosine kinase, BCR-ABL leukaemia and a German canon-law journal. **`ARMR` had never been probed by this series and is unusable**, returning the MarR-family antirepressor ArmR, a medication-recommendation network, annual ryegrass-maize rotation, the American Registry for Migraine Research, array-reader magnetic recording and an anonymous routing protocol, which is six fields and no aerospace. **Even the full expansion is not an anchor**, since `Affordable Responsive Modular Rocket` returns affordable housing in Singapore and responsive architecture. `RS1` returns the retinoschisin gene, a ginsenoside, a wine bacterium and a cryocooler. **`Invocon` and `Troy7` each return nothing at all**, which is a measurement about the sibling designation's contractors rather than a failure of the probe.

### The Store, and Which Families Were Opened

The shared rejection store holds 728 per-record judgements and 141 pattern lessons across 31 tagged families. **A family is opened against records and never against its name**, so the cost of each candidate was measured on this pool before anything was switched off.

- `missiles` releases 142 records from this pool, 60 of which the subject gate would admit. It is **opened**.
- `ramjet` releases 134 records from this pool, 75 of which the subject gate would admit. It is **left armed**.
- `hypersonics` releases 373 records from this pool, 204 of which the subject gate would admit. It is **opened**.

**The decision on `ramjet` was the close one and it was settled by reading the records rather than by counting them.** Of the 75 it releases that this gate would admit, 28 land in a nozzle or plume cluster and every one of those is the exhaust nozzle of an air-breathing engine, being a single expansion ramp expanding onto a hypersonic afterbody. **That is external expansion and it is not altitude compensation**, because its design driver is afterbody integration at flight Mach number rather than a falling ambient pressure. The remaining 47 are combustors, inlets, ducted rockets and combined cycles. **This vehicle has no inlet**, so the family stays armed and the cost of that is stated here rather than hidden.

**Two families were deliberately left armed and both are load-bearing here.** `fracture` was earned by A335 against parachute opening loads and tagged by A352 for bonded composite joints, and it is the only thing in this repository standing between this sweep and the fatigue-crack-closure literature, which shares both of its words with this nozzle's central flow feature. `wind-energy` was earned by A341 and A347 against rotor aerodynamics, and it is what refuses the wind-turbine thrust coefficient. **Neither was written with anything like this article in mind, and each turns out to guard the collision this article could least afford.**

### What the Award Record Was Asked, and What It Returned

**12 keywords were put to the federal award reporting system across 4 families of award type**, being procurement contracts, indefinite delivery vehicles, grants and two classes of other financial assistance. **7 of the 12 returned nothing in any family**, and they include `ABL Space Systems`, `ARISE aerospike`, `Aerospike Rocket Integration and Suborbital Experiment` and `Affordable Responsive Modular Rocket`. **The announcement explains the silence**, because the instrument used was an other transaction agreement through the Space Enterprise Consortium and not a procurement contract, and an other transaction does not appear where procurement contracts appear.

**One keyword returned a great deal and it is the sibling designation's.** Searching the recipient name of the X-64A team returns decades of instrumentation work for the space agency and the services, which is a fact about that company rather than about this programme, and it belongs to the article about that number.

### What This Article Read in Full

**Five primary documents were retrieved, saved and read end to end**, and every quotation in this article comes from one of them. They are the laboratory's public fact sheet for the programme, the two-page cleared version of the same document carrying its distribution statement, the award announcement as reprinted verbatim by the base newspaper, the manufacturer's payload user's guide of June 2022, and the manufacturer's own static-fire incident report of 26 August 2024. **The register itself was saved as markup and re-parsed twice by different routines**, because the officiality classification this article corrects depends on which element carries a class attribute rather than on any visible text.

**Three official mirrors of the award announcement return 403 to every fetcher tried**, which is the documented behaviour of that domain and not evidence about the document. The version cited is a verbatim reprint carrying the same byline and date, and its text was compared against the portions quoted in independent summaries.

## Epistemic State

**Facts, taken from primary documents and stated as they appear there.** The two designations, their shared date of 20 April 2022, their sponsor cell, their engines cell and their identical 101-character description come from the register \[[DOD 4120.15-L Addendum][ref_mds_addendum]\]. The programme's objectives, the three wake regimes, the modular architecture and the clearance number come from the laboratory's own fact sheet \[[ARISE and Fly][ref_afrl_arise]\]. The December 2019 award date, the three-year term, the other transaction instrument, the scope wording, the promise of thrust vector control and the three quotations come from the award announcement \[[AFRL awards agreements under ARISE][ref_arise_award]\]. The vehicle's dimensions, propellants, cycle, engine counts, thrust figures and reference mission come from the manufacturer's payload user's guide \[[ABL Payload User's Guide][ref_abl_pug]\]. The static fire date, the eleven engines, Engine 10, the 4.5 kilohertz first tangential mode, the erosion of two injectors, the three hundred prior tests and the whole loss timeline come from the manufacturer's incident report \[[Flight 2 Static Fire Update][ref_abl_staticfire]\].

**Derivations, which follow from the facts by mathematics and are checked numerically.** The affine dependence of thrust on ambient pressure, the conjugacy of ambient pressure and exit area, the Legendre structure of the envelope, the identification of the fixed-nozzle loss as a Bregman divergence, and the rule that the optimal fixed nozzle expands to the burn-averaged ambient pressure are all exact. The conjugacy identity was checked by central differences in twelve cases to 2.1 parts in a hundred thousand million. The mean-in-time rule was checked in one hundred independent optimisations to 4.2 parts in ten million. The ring formulae were checked against a direct directional search in forty-two cases to below one part in a million million.

**Quantities that depend on assumptions, with the assumptions swept and the spread reported.** The burn-averaged ambient pressure depends on an ascent profile fitted to two published points, and runs from 19.4 to 41.6 percent of sea level across the family used. The impulse gain of an ideal spike over the best fixed nozzle runs from 5.3 to 8.5 percent across ratios of specific heats from 1.20 to 1.24 and chamber pressures from 3 to 10 megapascal. The recovered chamber diameter runs from 147 to 179 millimetres across forty-eight combinations of gas properties, and the recovered chamber pressure from 2.6 to 8.7 megapascal across thirty-six further combinations.

**Inferences, marked as such where they appear.** That the fact sheet's phrase about a launch-to-orbit trajectory means a representative trajectory rather than an orbital flight. That the 133,118 pound force total thrust in a nine-engine row is the eleven-engine figure. That the X-63A programme has ended. That the ARISE engine's modules, if arranged on a ring, would obey the parity result. **None of these is stated as a fact anywhere in this article and each is reversible by one document.**

**Two conflicts in the sources are recorded and not resolved.** The maximum payload of the RS1 is given as 1,200 kilograms in the award announcement and 1,350 kilograms in the launch-vehicle reference. And the programme is named a suborbital experiment while its own fact sheet describes a launch-to-orbit trajectory.

**One correction to this series' own arithmetic.** A358 gave the X-row officiality split as 21 official and 9 not, which accounts for 30 of 31 rows because the register's third category has nowhere to go in a two-number summary. A359 closed the sum by raising the official count to 22, which places the partly marked row on the side its markup denies. The correct three-way split, recomputed here from the saved page and reproduced by an independent re-parse of the underlying markup, is **21 official, 9 wholly unofficial and 1 partly unofficial**. **The register-wide figures A358 gave, 86 and a further 17, are exactly right.**

**One dateline limit.** The encyclopedia entry cited for the X-63A's history carries a revision date of 17 December 2025, which is nine days after this article's date. Every statement drawn from it concerns events well before that, and the inference about cancellation is made here in this article's own voice rather than adopted from it. **The web archive was unreachable when this was checked, so the page's earlier state could not be inspected**, and that is a limit rather than a resolution.

**What is not known and would change things.** The module count and arrangement of the ARISE engine. The chamber pressure and area ratio of the aerospike as designed. Whether any hardware was built. The dollar value of either agreement. And whether the X-64A, which shares every word of its description with this one, ever reached a different stage.

## Out of Scope

**The X-64A is a separate article.** The Invocon team's vehicle is described as recoverable, landing on four legs that double as stabilising fins, about twelve metres tall and two and a half metres in diameter, and the measurement problem it exists to solve is a different one. It is deliberately left alone here beyond the fact that its designation was issued on the same day for the same words.

**The internal aerodynamics of the plug contour are not treated.** Designing the spike surface is a method-of-characteristics problem with a large literature and it does not bear on the questions asked here.

**Base heating, cooling and structural mass are named and not computed**, for the reason given above, which is that none of them can be obtained from the model this article uses.

**Nothing here is a judgement about whether the money was well spent.** The programme bought a flight that did not happen, from a company that left the business, on an instrument that leaves no public trace of its value. Those are three facts and they do not add up to an assessment.

## Conclusion

**Two X numbers were issued on one day with one description, and the description does not say which vehicle is which.**

The thing both were built to fly is older than almost everyone working on it and has never flown. This article's account of why is that the prize is real, bounded and awkwardly sized. **An ideal altitude-compensating nozzle is worth between five and eight percent of first-stage impulse on this vehicle's own published trajectory**, measured against the best fixed nozzle that trajectory admits, and that is a large number for a launch vehicle and a small one against the cost of a new nozzle architecture.

**The mathematics is tidier than the hardware.** Thrust is affine in ambient pressure with slope minus the exit area. The incremental vacuum thrust from an increment of exit area is exactly the exit pressure, which makes ambient pressure and exit area conjugate variables. **The ideal spike's thrust curve is the Legendre transform of the vacuum thrust, every fixed nozzle is one of its tangent lines, and the loss of a fixed nozzle is a Bregman divergence.** From the same identity comes the design rule, which is that **the optimal fixed nozzle expands to the time-averaged ambient pressure of its own flight**, a statement containing nothing about the gas, the engine or the vehicle.

**And that rule is what makes the case.** On this trajectory the burn-averaged ambient pressure is 28.06 percent of sea level under the constant-acceleration model and between 19.4 and 41.6 percent across the family of ascent profiles tried, half of the whole pressure-time integral is collected in the first 17.6 to 34.0 seconds of a hundred and sixty second burn, and the optimal nozzle therefore sits at an exit-to-ambient ratio at liftoff equal to that burn-averaged fraction, which is 0.2806 for the central case. **That is inside the band where an over-expanded nozzle separates from its own wall.** The best fixed nozzle for this flight is one that cannot be lit at sea level without accepting separation, and an aerospike does not have the problem because it has no divergent wall to separate from.

**The other half of the programme yields a second exact result and it points the other way.** Differential throttling of a ring of modules gives a directional average authority of exactly the throttle depth divided by pi, at every module count from three upward, so more modules buy evenness rather than authority. **The evenness depends on parity, because an odd ring has no diametrically opposite pair and its control polygon therefore has two sides per module instead of one.** Nine modules steer as evenly as eighteen and better than any even count below twenty. **After a failure the ranking reverses**, because a failure breaks the symmetry the parity argument rests on, and then what matters is only how many are left.

**The programme did not fly.** The first vehicle of the parent design failed 10.87 seconds after liftoff, the second burned on the pad while the water ran out, and the company renamed itself and went into missile defence. The register still carries both numbers, side by side, with the same hundred and one characters against each. **Nothing in it records that the two rows were ever anything but equal.**
